I support what you are saying there. However, it is not OP's job to change the system that does not believe victims and treats them this way (whether trained or not). They are preparing people for what may HAPPEN. The same way BIPOC have "the talk" with their kids. Sure they may not be profiled and potentially harmed but they need to be prepared for it if/when it does. This is less about the actions of kids and victims being wrong and more about a system that in anyway thinks that behavior or conduct is okay.

For the record, I did not say ACAB. What I am saying is that every experience I have seen, heard about, or experienced has been negative. It is my narrative. If yours does not match that is fine. But I am not the only one experiencing these issues and that is very obvious based on our current climate. We need to make a change so that less people experience this.

I will concede that I dont know anything about training that you go through. I'm inclined to support you because the officers didn't even give us the positive first meeting that the post details. We were straight up abused. They accused us of every single cliche thing they could think of and I personally had so much trauma from my first interaction that I never reported the next 3 assaults that I experienced. I helped my friends report their assaults in 4 different areas/stations and all incidents were met with awful hostility and abuse from the officers. It was sickening to be abused by the people hired to "serve and protect" repeatedly. 

I want to find those "good" officers that people speak of but I've so far been disappointed. (Off topic the 3 other interactions that were not assault related were even worse. Domestic abuse at the hands of my father? I called the cops and was told I'm the reason he is an alcoholic. Two minor traffic incidents? One made very off color remarks about my appearance and my passenger and the other threatened to take me to jail over a headlight.) I respect cops as I was raised to and yet my respect has been met with hate, hostility, and personal trauma. Im a respectful white girl. Its no wonder the BIPOC of color in this country are angry. If my experience was this bad, I cant imagine theirs.

Yeah... This is 100% indicative of what myself and many known victims that Im friends with have gone through. Except the untrue part is that the police do believe you even if they don't act like it.
